I put $50 into $LAB in one wallet and $30 into another.

The $30 wallet finished with more money in it.

Same token, same call, same entry window. Here is the only difference.

I swing traded the smaller wallet harder.

Every local pump got sold. Every dip got bought back.

By the time $LAB was done it had run 353x from where I called it in October.

Most people in this market have one gear: buy it, sit on it, wait for the top.

Then the top does not look like they imagined, they hold through the round trip, and they finish the cycle with the same token count they started with.

Here is how it compounds instead.

When something runs, I take profits on the way up and rotate the dry powder into the other plays I am already tracking. 200 here, 100 there, 300 somewhere else.

So the next time one of them goes parabolic, I am not 350x-ing $80.

I am 350x-ing $500.

The wins get bigger because the last win paid for them.

The receipts: 353x on $LAB. 58x on Velvet. 30x on Giggle Fund.

And $TUT, called in September, ran 94x, looked like a total rug, then came back to 130x and printed a new all time high. I sold the top and bought back lower.

The catch: you cannot run this on vibes. If you cannot track it, hold fewer tokens. Five is plenty.

Never financial advice.

That is the part nobody wants to sit with. The people calling for 1.4 cents are describing a chart, not the holders standing behind it.

Look at what the last four years actually did. Kaspa came out of a fair launch nobody was allowed to front run, ground its way down to around 2.5 cents, and dragged everybody through a bear that broke most of the conviction in this market. The people who were going to capitulate did it already. Some of them got in at a fraction of a cent, watched a 10x, and gave up anyway, because four bad years teaches you to grab any green you can find.

So when I hear 1.4 cents, my honest answer is: maybe. I have the line drawn. I am not going to pretend I can time the wick. What I am not going to do is sit on the sidelines waiting for a number that might never print, and then watch it leave without me. If you want to DCA, DCA. Never financial advice.

Because the thing underneath the price has not moved at all.

Kaspa is a fully implemented GhostDAG. 5,700 TPS against Bitcoin's 7. No premine, no VC allocation, no foundation bag waiting to hit you on the way up. It is not on Coinbase because there was no premine to fund the listing, and that exclusion is the receipt, not the flaw.

It is a super upgraded Bitcoin. Nothing on the board is close, and I do not think it gets properly repriced until we are in a real cycle top, not the rinky dink version we got handed in 2025.

When people tell me Kaspa does 5x from here, my reaction is that the number is small. That is my opinion, never financial advice.

And when Kaspa moves, the KRC20s move harder. I am still holding mine.

yt_posts.topic: Swing trading: the $30 wallet that won
yt_posts.body:
I put $50 into $LAB in one wallet and $30 into another. The $30 wallet finished with more money in it.

Same token. Same call. Same entry window. The only difference was that I swing traded the smaller wallet harder, and by the time $LAB was done it had run 353x from where I called it in October.

That is the whole lesson, and it is worth more than any single call I have ever made.

Most people in this market have one gear: buy it, sit on it, wait for the top. Then the top does not look like they imagined, they hold straight through the round trip, and they finish a cycle with the same number of tokens they started with. Meanwhile the person selling every local pump and buying the dip back finishes the same move with double, triple, quadruple the bag.

Here is how it compounds. When something runs, I take profits on the way up and rotate the dry powder into the other plays I am already tracking. 200 here, 100 there, 300 somewhere else. So the next time one of them goes parabolic, I am not 350x-ing $80, I am 350x-ing $500. The wins get bigger because the last win paid for them.

The receipts on that loop: 353x on $LAB. 58x on Velvet, which is in retracement right now and took 11 months from the call. 30x on Giggle Fund. And $TUT, called in September, ran 94x, looked like a total rug on the chart, then came back to 130x and printed a new all time high. I sold into the top and bought back lower, so the bag is bigger now than it was during the 94x.

The catch is you cannot run this on vibes. I did it in spreadsheets until the start of last year and it nearly drove me insane, so I built software that tracks every wallet, every entry, every partial. That is what my community uses.

If you cannot track it, hold fewer tokens. Five is plenty. Ten or fifteen if you are degen and organized. Never financial advice.

So which one are you: do you swing trade your bags, or do you sit and wait for the top?

Hit like and subscribe if this is the kind of breakdown you want more of.
